Subject: Arcadia MAP kickoff — internal prep & roles

Team —

We have the Arcadia MAP kickoff with Jordan Ellis (Arcadia) next week. Goal here is to align internally so the kickoff feels crisp and we present a defensible evaluation plan and close timeline. Outlined asks below: 

1) Confirm internal roles (owner / approver / technical lead / SRE contact).
2) Review the attached MAP draft (Arcadia_MAP_v0.3.xlsx) for completeness — look for missing milestones and any unrealistic dates.
3) Note evaluation criteria: latency SLA, inference cost per QPS, data residency controls, and an integration POC. Monica will own the rubric but please flag anything missing.
4) Confirm primary Arcadia stakeholders (we expect Jordan = executive sponsor; procurement contact included below).
5) Please add any legal/contract blockers you foresee — Marcus, can you call out redline risk areas?

Target close: internal goal is EOW 2026-09-30 (commercial close). We’re proposing a MAP timeline that targets a 6-week eval window starting 2026-09-06 to leave room for procurement and any legal cycles. If that feels tight, say so now.

Action: Reply with confirmations/edits by EOD Tue Aug 17 so I can lock version 0.3 before the pre-kick prep call. I’ll schedule an internal 30-min sync Wed 8/18 10:00am PT unless someone flags a conflict.

Thanks —
Hannah

Sounds good. A couple quick points: 

- Please add Arcadia procurement contact (procurement@arcadia-sys.com) to the external stakeholder list in the doc — they tend to be our gating factor for net-30 vs net-60.
- Legal will want to see our data residency and deletion commitments up front; I recommend we pre-run the contract redline checklist and mark the clauses we expect to push on. I can draft the expected redlines and circulate by Tue morning.
- For evaluation, include a short POC acceptance test (3 clear pass/fail items) so Arcadia knows when the eval is 'done'. Monica, can you add that to the rubric?

If procurement / legal timelines elongate, we should surface a fallback (short-term hosted trial with limited data) in the MAP.

—Marcus
